text:
oliver: Heads up — since last night we're seeing a spike in GPU provisioning failures in eu-west3. Node boot logs show local NVMe IOPS saturation + checksum alerts. Provisioning latency jumped from ~8s -> ~45s, lots of OOM killer traces.

lina: Linking the alert: https://ops/alerts/PROV-324 :eyes:

oliver: Logs snippet:
```
[gnode-54] nvme0: SMART_EVENT data_integrity_error=1
[janitor] deltmp: rm -rf /scratch/tmp/... exit(0)
kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
```

raj: Are these the nodes running scrub/janitor at same time as GPU batch? Might be janitor concurrency.

marta: Yes — janitor window overlapped with nightly bundle-prewarm. Janitor concurrency was set to 32 yesterday.

oliver: We correlated: when janitor_concurrency >=16, provision fail rate -> +6%. When we lowered to 4 in a canary AZ it stabilized.

sre-oncall: Oncall plan: throttle janitor to 2 in eu-west3 now, and add node prechecks to reject nodes with SMART flags. Will patch shortly.

janitor-bot: executing: set-concurrency --service janitor --region eu-west3 --concurrency 2 :hammer:

lina: Patch for pre-provision check is in PR #6212 — small script to read nvme smart and failfast on crc/readonly flags.

raj: We should also consider increasing the provisioning timeout and prefer nodes with freshest drives (tag: nvme-fresh=true). Otherwise autoscaler keeps trying stale nodes.

marta: Cost note — lowering janitor concurrency increases background backlog; might push us to more reserved writes later. Tradeoff is short-term reliability vs longer-term wear cost.

oliver: For customer impact — we've diverted 90% of requests to us-west2 for now. Need decision: keep janitor throttled for 12h and run a targeted scrub resume at low concurrency overnight?

sre-oncall: Agreed. I'll leave throttled for 12h and schedule the resume at 03:00 UTC with concurrency 1. Also adding a fallback route to dedicated-pool eu-west3-d1.

marta: Open question: firmware patch from vendor rolled last week — did that change GC behavior? Logs show increased background GC ops.

raj: Good catch. Reverting firmware on a small canary could prove/disprove. cc: infra-firmware.

oliver: Final ask: can infra-firmware do a one-node canary rollback tonight? If yes we'll run telemetry for 6h and then decide.

sre-oncall: Ack. filing ticket INFRA-879 and tagging infra-firmware. :white_check_mark:
